book.overgeared.guide.page.1:
§0§l§4Overgeared§0
§8A Blacksmith's Guide§0

Tools and armor are no longer made at a crafting table. You knap, heat, hammer and polish them yourself.

The better your work, the better the gear.
book.overgeared.guide.page.2:
§0§lContents§0
1. Rocks & Knapping
2. Tool Heads
3. Hot Metal
4. Hammers & Anvils
5. Forging
6. Quality
7. Polishing
8. Blueprints
9. Steel & Alloys
10. Casting
11. Diamond Gear
12. Arrows
13. Breaking
book.overgeared.guide.page.3:
§0§l1. Rocks & Knapping§0

Right-click stone with §1Flint§0 to chip off §1Rocks§0. The stone may crack into cobblestone, and the flint can break.

Hold a Rock in each hand and right-click to start §1knapping§0.
book.overgeared.guide.page.4:
§0§lKnapping§0

Click squares on the 3x3 grid to chip them away for good. Leave this shape:
§8Pickaxe:§0 row of 3
§8Axe:§0 L of 3
§8Sword:§0 2 stacked
§8Shovel:§0 1
§8Hoe:§0 2 side by side
§8Spear:§0 a ^ point of 3
book.overgeared.guide.page.5:
§0§l2. Tool Heads§0

Every tool is a §1tool head + stick§0.

Stone heads come from knapping. Iron, copper, gold and steel heads are §1forged§0 on an anvil.

Armor is forged from metal §1plates§0.
book.overgeared.guide.page.6:
§0§l3. Hot Metal§0

Smelt ingots in a §1Blast Furnace§0 to heat them. Most metal must be §cheated§0 before you can forge it.

Carrying hot metal burns you! Hold §1Tongs§0 in either hand to stay safe. Fire Resistance also protects you.
book.overgeared.guide.page.7:
§0§lTongs§0

§8Wooden:§0 5 sticks in a plus shape.
§8Iron / Steel:§0 forge two single tongs from heated ingots, then combine them.

Tongs wear down slowly while they protect you.
book.overgeared.guide.page.8:
§0§lCooling§0

Hot metal cools down after a minute in your inventory.

To cool it right away, §1right-click a water cauldron§0 while holding it, or drop it into water.

Cool forged heads before using them.
book.overgeared.guide.page.9:
§0§l4. Hammers & Anvils§0

Craft a §1Smithing Hammer§0 from a hammer head and a stick. A copper hammer can also be made from 2 copper ingots and 2 sticks.

Hammers wear down with every strike.
book.overgeared.guide.page.10:
§0§lMaking an Anvil§0

§1Sneak + right-click§0 with a hammer:

§8Stone§0: §1Stone Anvil§0. Basic recipes, max Well quality, breaks after 64 uses.

§8Anvil§0: §1Smithing Anvil§0. All recipes and blueprints.
book.overgeared.guide.page.11:
§0§l5. Forging§0

Right-click an anvil to open it. Put the ingredients in the 3x3 grid and a hammer in its slot.

Simple recipes like plates just need a few right-clicks on the anvil with your hammer.
book.overgeared.guide.page.12:
§0§lThe Minigame§0

§1Sneak + right-click§0 the anvil with a hammer to begin.

Right-click to strike when the arrow is in the §2good§0 or §6perfect§0 zone.

Each strike speeds up the arrow and shrinks the zones.
book.overgeared.guide.page.13:
§0§l6. Quality§0

Your strikes decide the quality:

§cPoorly Forged§0
§0Well Forged§0
§9Expertly Forged§0
§6Perfectly Forged§0
§5Masterwork§0

Perfect results have a small chance to become Masterwork.
book.overgeared.guide.page.14:
§0§lWhat Quality Does§0

Better quality means more durability, mining speed and damage, and stronger armor.

Poor gear is weaker than normal.

The best quality of your ingredients also caps the result.
book.overgeared.guide.page.15:
§0§l7. Polishing§0

Forged heads come out §8unpolished§0. §1Sneak + right-click a grindstone§0 to polish them.

Unpolished or hot heads make a lower quality tool.

Polish §cafter§0 cooling, or lose a tier!
book.overgeared.guide.page.16:
§0§lRepairing§0

Sneak + right-click a grindstone with damaged gear to repair some durability.

Each repair lowers its max durability a little.

Grind a §1Diamond§0 into §1Diamond Shards§0.
book.overgeared.guide.page.17:
§0§l8. Blueprints§0

Craft an §1Empty Blueprint§0 (3 paper + blue dye) and a §1Drafting Table§0.

Use the table to pick a tool type and draw a blueprint.

Put it in the Smithing Anvil's blueprint slot while forging that tool.
book.overgeared.guide.page.18:
§0§lBlueprint Quality§0

Without a blueprint, tool heads max out at Well quality. A blueprint raises the limit to its own quality.

Expert or better forges level it up.

Wandering Traders sell rare blueprints.
book.overgeared.guide.page.19:
§0§lCopying Blueprints§0

Craft a blueprint with an empty blueprint to get two copies.

Each copy is one quality tier lower than the original.
book.overgeared.guide.page.20:
§0§l9. Steel & Alloys§0

Mix §13 iron + 1 coal§0 in an Alloy Furnace to get Crude Steel.

Heat it in a Blast Furnace, then forge it on a §1Smithing Anvil§0 into a Steel Ingot.

Steel gear sits between iron and diamond.
book.overgeared.guide.page.21:
§0§lAlloy Furnaces§0

§1Alloy Furnace:§0 8 bricks around a blast furnace. 4 input slots.

§1Nether Alloy Furnace:§0 8 nether bricks around a blast furnace. 9 slots.

Both burn normal fuel.
book.overgeared.guide.page.22:
§0§lNetherite§0

Smelt §14 netherite scrap + 4 gold§0 in the Nether Alloy Furnace.

Forge the hot alloy on a Smithing Anvil. It takes 10 hard strikes, and failing gives back the scrap.
book.overgeared.guide.page.23:
§0§l10. Casting§0

Surround a tool head with 4 §1clay balls§0 (or 4 nether bricks) in a crafting grid. You get your head back plus a §1Tool Cast§0.

Fire a clay cast in a furnace before use.

Casts copy heads at one quality tier lower.
book.overgeared.guide.page.24:
§0§lFilling a Cast§0

Right-click ingots or nuggets onto the cast in your inventory.

Smelt it in a furnace or §1Casting Furnace§0, then right-click it to take the head out.

Clay casts wear out. Nether casts never do.
book.overgeared.guide.page.25:
§0§l11. Diamond Gear§0

Diamond tools and armor are upgraded from §1steel gear§0 at a Smithing Table.

You need a §1Diamond Upgrade Smithing Template§0. Find it in chests in strongholds, temples, and other structures.
book.overgeared.guide.page.26:
§0§l12. Arrows§0

Use a §1Fletching Table§0 to make arrows from a tip, shaft and feather.

Iron, steel and diamond tips deal more damage.

Add a potion to tip them. Lingering potions make lingering arrows.
book.overgeared.guide.page.27:
§0§l13. Breaking§0

Gear that runs out of durability may become §cBroken§0 instead of breaking, and drop a quality tier.

Broken gear is useless until repaired.

Better quality gear breaks less often.
book.overgeared.guide.page.28:
§0§lFinal Tips§0

Use §1JEI§0 to look up every forging recipe.

Lost this book? Run §1/overgeared guide§0 for a new copy.

Good luck, smith!
